signalsmachines:usageinfo-signalsmachine: Signals Machines - machines that will work for you

Signals Machines
Machines controlled by signals of the Signals mod, which can do various jobs for you automatically - but not for free.

What a machine cannot do by itself
It is not enough to build the machine and wait for it to do everything for you. Every machine is a state machine: it has input pins it is controlled through, and an output pin that reports its state. What it lacks is a controller - and that you have to build yourself, by wiring a Signals network that gives the machine the right commands at the right moment and reacts to its reports. You have to rack and strain your brain and work it out. Your reward for that effort is a machine that works well.
For full automation the other mods of the SignalsLink family will come in handy: SignalsLink with its managed chutes, dampers and hoses moves items into the machines and takes the products away. You can then store the finished network in a program tube of Signals Tubes and seat it in the socket of every further copy of the same machine - no need to build the control again.

Machines
• Crafting machine - crafts whatever you lay on its plate, by crafting grid recipes. It needs mechanical power, a temporal crystal, and your sharp mind and ingenuity in building the Signals circuit that controls it. A mistake in the control shows as an explosion: the batch burns to burnt dust and temporal instability leaks into the surroundings.
signalsmachines:block-handbooktext-craft:
The crafting machine crafts by crafting grid recipes without a player. It is two blocks tall: a pedestal with the pins and a tube socket below, and above it the chamber with a turning 3x3 plate, the crystal and a door on each of two opposite sides. The drive axle enters the back wall of the pedestal.

Pins (numbered like a Signals Tubes socket, front row 1-4, back row 5-8)
1 State (output) - reports what the machine is doing; values below.
2 Clutch (input) - a signal couples the plate to the drive; the plate takes about two seconds to spin up, and after release it comes to rest in its home position.
3 Crystal down (input) - a signal lowers the crystal over the plate. With a strength above 0 the crystal gives off temporal radiation.
4 Strength (input) - how much energy the crystal gives. While crafting it must equal exactly the number of occupied cells on the plate (1-9).
5 and 6 Doors (input) - each pin opens one of the chamber's side walls; which side of the world that is depends on how the machine is turned, and the pin's tooltip tells it. A door pushes out and slides down (about 2 s), closing takes about 3 s.
7 and 8 - reserve; switches and delays brought out of a tube use them.

A tube instead of wires
A program tube can be seated in the socket in the pedestal (right mouse button; an empty hand takes it out again). It then drives pins 2-6 and wires on them are ignored; the tube itself sees the State pin and the reserve pins. The imprinter's plug can be plugged straight into the machine's socket to imprint the network that controls the machine - the machine's pin names come prefilled in the tube.
Signals from outside through the reserve pins. A tube in the machine sees only the machine's pins. If the control circuit is to react to something outside - say a sensor watching the supply of ingredients, or a switch - a wire from the sensor into the circuit is not enough: when imprinting, such a sensor would stay beyond the border and the circuit would lose it. Run a wire from the sensor to a reserve pin of the machine (7 or 8) and another wire from that same pin into the control circuit. The reserve pin is then imprinted as an input of the tube, and once the tube is seated it carries the sensor's signal inside; the sensor stays connected to the pin. Send a signal out the same way - the circuit's output to a reserve pin, and from there a wire to a lamp or the next machine.

Loading and unloading
The chamber can only be reached through a door that is fully open, and only while the plate stands still (clutch released, plate at rest). By hand you right-click a cell of the plate: with an item in hand you put down one piece (the whole stack while sneaking), with an empty hand you take the cell's contents; the finished product floats in the middle of the chamber and is taken the same way. Managed chutes and dampers of SignalsLink can put items in and take them out - they point at the chamber from a door side and target single cells and the product, but they only get access while a door is open, on the same terms as a hand. The moment a door pin drops, access ends.

Crafting
The machine keeps looking for a crafting grid recipe in the layout on the plate; it shows the recipe it found in its tooltip. Recipes tied to a class are made by the class of the player who placed the machine. Crafting runs when the doors are closed, the product has been taken, the clutch is engaged, the plate is turning, the crystal is down and the strength equals the number of occupied cells. It takes 3 seconds plus one second per occupied cell. One run uses up what it can: the recipe repeats while the ingredients last and the product fits into one stack; tools in the recipe wear, returned items (such as empty containers) stay on the plate. An interrupted run waits 5 seconds, then the progress is lost.

States on pin 1
0 waiting - no recipe on the plate, or a door is open.
1 recipe ready - doors closed, recipe recognised, output empty, no control input active.
2 preparing - some input is active, but not all conditions for crafting are met yet; also a pause of a started run.
3 crafting.
4 done - the product waits to be taken and there is no further recipe on the plate.
10 overloaded - the strength rose by 3 or more in one step, or with the crystal down it was greater than the number of cells + 1. The crystal exploded and the batch burned to burnt dust.
11 crystal down, plate still - for more than 1 s.
12 door opened while crafting - the run is lost, the batch stays.
13 wrong strength - strength greater than the number of cells for more than 2 s with the crystal down.
14 output full - the product waits and the next recipe already lies on the plate.
15 no drive - clutch engaged and the drive network standing still for more than 3 s.
Errors 10-13 and 15 hold until the strength is 0, the crystal is up and the clutch is released. State 14 clears when the product is taken. Raise the strength step by step, at most by 2 per step; after a tube is seated or taken out the machine forgives the first change.

Drive
The plate turns only with a mechanical network running at 30 % of its speed or more; one large windmill is enough. A standing network with the clutch engaged is error 15 after 3 s.

Instability
A lowered crystal works with temporal instability. While crafting it raises it slightly within two blocks. If you open a door while the crystal is radiating, temporal smog leaks out of the chamber: it flows out of the door along the ground like a heavy gas, covers up to eight blocks, raises the instability sharply for anyone standing in it, and fades away about a minute after the door closes. An overload releases the strongest smog. So open the doors only with the crystal dark.
signalsmachines:item-handbooktext-burntd: What is left after a crafting machine overloads: a pile of dust for every occupied cell of the plate. It is good for nothing, but it reminds you that the crystal's strength goes up in steps, and never above the number of cells on the plate.
